suites.label: PFN-DiD · 2,000-table Test
suites.aggregation: Direct transcription of the reported 2,000-set Test summary. Both methods completed all 2,000 sets from 13 DGPs, each with 500 units. The website does not combine earlier training seeds or reconstruct results from the previous experiment.
suites.variance_definition: Sample variance of population-ATT estimation errors across the 2,000 sets, with denominator 1,999. Not a within-mechanism repeated-sampling variance.
suites.protocol: Both methods use identical five-fold splits and the same normalized DR-DiD score for ATT. PFN-DiD: frozen TabPFN-3.5 backbone, separate width-8 residual bottleneck adapters after the last four ICL blocks for propensity scores and untreated outcome changes; training seed 20261112, checkpoint step 8500. RF: classification forest for propensity scores on training-fold units; regression forest for untreated outcome change on training-fold controls; 200 trees and minimum leaf size 5. PFN uses influence-function standard errors. RF uses standard errors from 50 full row-bootstrap refits including re-splitting. Both report 95% normal intervals; the RF interval is not a percentile interval.

intervals.pfn: 95% normal interval using influence-function standard error
intervals.rf: 95% normal interval using standard error from B=50 complete row-bootstrap refits; not percentile

suites.sample_design: 2,000 sets from 13 DGPs; 500 units per set; same original five-fold splits and all sets completed for both methods.
suites.caveat: The source supplies pooled results, not per-DGP metrics. The normalized DR-DiD score does not mean the displayed errors were divided by SD(Y): the report defines errors as estimated minus true population ATT.

suites.label: Normalized units · Nov 16, 2026

source.title: Proximal causal inference — unified-protocol evaluation
source.locators: Page 4: normalized summary and mechanism results; page 6: original-unit results; pages 3 and 8: protocol and timing; page 10: references

suites.aggregation: Directly reported summary over 2,000 equally weighted paired tasks, without ID/OOD groups. For each task, estimation error and interval length are divided by that original table’s sample SD(Y), ddof=1, before aggregation. Coverage and time are unchanged. Mechanism counts are 496 (Cui linear), 516 (Qi linear heterogeneous), 510 (Qi quadratic) and 478 (Qi trigonometric); the reported overall values are not recomputed from rounded mechanism rows.
suites.variance_definition: Sample variance of per-task standardized errors e_i / s_i with denominator N−1 = 1,999; s_i is the original 500-row sample SD(Y). This crosses randomly sampled mechanisms, parameters, queries and observations; it is not fixed-mechanism sampling variance.
suites.protocol: ProximalFM uses the frozen official checkpoint with fold_context_mixture: five 400-row contexts defined by shared original K=5 labels produce five CATE distributions at the same independent query. Point estimate is the equal-weight mixture mean; the 95% interval uses the discrete mixture CDF quantiles, not averaged endpoints or SE/√5. This is context-fold ensembling, not nuisance cross-fitting or the official native_full default. RF + bootstrap is the project-specific proximal series-IV/sieve-GMM baseline, not a P-learner reproduction: scikit-learn 1.7.2, 200 trees, min_samples_leaf=5, n_jobs=1, other estimator defaults apart from seed. Five-fold out-of-fold E[W,W²|A,X,Z] predictions feed a 20-column quadratic bridge/GMM; ridge=1e-4 and instrument ridge=1e-6. Standardization, final bridge and W|X query forest use the full table. B=50 IID whole-row resamples each re-split K=5 and refit the entire pipeline; duplicate rows may enter different new folds as reported. RF interval is the linear-interpolated 2.5%/97.5% percentile interval. No failed bootstrap draw is discarded or replaced.

intervals.pfn: 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles of the five-context discrete distribution mixture
intervals.rf: B=50 full-pipeline row-bootstrap percentile interval; NumPy linear quantiles

suites.sample_design: 2,000 frozen tasks from four adapted literature mechanisms; n=500; one independent query CATE per task. All 4,000 method records and 100,000 bootstrap refits completed; no observations or tasks were trimmed.
notes: Bias, Variance, RMSE and Length are normalized per task by the original table’s sample SD(Y). Select Original units to view the reported unnormalized results.
suites.caveat: Overall ProximalFM coverage is 96.50%, but Qi quadratic coverage is 89.61% (457/510). RF has long-tailed errors, and 39.75% of original-table point estimates lie outside their percentile intervals. PFN mixture credible intervals and RF bootstrap intervals have different interpretations. Four mechanisms share a Gaussian proxy skeleton; results do not cover every proximal task. Source DGP scientific review remains needs_scientific_review; engineering integrity checks are not independent scientific validation.

suites.timing: Warm mean seconds per task on a shared Linux AMD EPYC 9755 CPU server with 224 visible logical CPUs; no GPU. source.title: CausalPFN and Random Forest for ATE and CATE — Evaluation on a Fixed Collection of Synthetic Test Mechanisms
source.locators: Page 3, Table 2 (overall results); pages 1–2 (scope and methods); pages 7–9 (timing and reproducibility).

suites.aggregation: Direct transcription of Table 2, with equal weight for each of the 13 DGP families. The fixed collection contains 1,000 parameterized mechanisms and two independent 500-row datasets per mechanism. ATE and CATE use the same 2,000 datasets; no ID/OOD pooling or recomputation from rounded family results is performed by the website.
suites.variance_definition: Source-reported within-mechanism sampling variance from paired independently sampled datasets, aggregated with equal DGP-family weights. Transcribed directly from the Variance column, not reconstructed from SE or substituted with cross-task error variance.
suites.protocol: CausalPFN 0.1.5 with unchanged official causalpfn_v0.pt weights and calibrate=False; native point and interval workflows with 10,000 predictive draws, alpha=0.05, and no additional five-fold wrapper. RF uses scikit-learn 1.7.2, 200 trees, min_samples_leaf=5, n_jobs=1 and fixed seeds. ATE uses treatment-stratified five-fold AIPW with propensity clipping to [0.01,0.99]; CATE uses a five-fold T-learner ensemble. RF percentile intervals use 50 full row-bootstrap refits with new grouped, treatment-stratified folds; duplicates of an original row remain in one fold. CATE query remains fixed.
suites.timing: Family-weighted mean warm wall-clock seconds per dataset–target task, including point estimation and interval construction. RF includes the original fit and all 50 bootstrap refits. Excludes checkpoint loading, warm-up, data generation, I/O, scheduling waits and checkpoint saving. CausalPFN uses four NVIDIA L40 GPUs; RF uses 216 single-thread outer workers from a 224-CPU allocation. Different hardware and workloads; no controlled same-hardware speedup is asserted.
suites.sample_design: 13 families; 1,000 mechanisms; 2,000 paired datasets; n=500; dimension 2–10; shared data and fixed mechanism-specific CATE queries across methods. Every point estimate and interval is reported valid.
